title: Go: Environment Config
description: Read environment variables and use the flag package to configure Go applications.

steps.title: os.Getenv
steps.description: Read the `HOME` environment variable with `os.Getenv("HOME")` and print "HOME: <value>". Also print `GOPATH` in the same way.
hints: `os.Getenv(key)` returns the value as a string
If the variable is not set, Getenv returns empty string

verification.failureMessage: Pass the variable name as a string to os.Getenv.

steps.title: os.LookupEnv
steps.description: Use `os.LookupEnv("MY_APP_PORT")` to check if a variable exists. If it does, print "PORT: <value>". If not, print "MY_APP_PORT not set".
hints: The bool is true if the variable is set (even if empty)
Use this when you need to distinguish "unset" from "empty"

verification.failureMessage: Use the boolean return value from LookupEnv.

steps.title: Default values
steps.description: Write a helper `getEnv(key, defaultVal string) string` that returns the env value or a default if not set. Use it to get a `DB_HOST` (default "localhost") and print the result.
hints: Check with `os.LookupEnv` — if not set, return defaultValue
Return value if found, otherwise defaultValue

verification.failureMessage: Use LookupEnv inside your helper function.

steps.title: Parsing to types
steps.description: Read `WORKERS` env var (default "4") and parse it to an int using `strconv.Atoi`. Print the value and the type using `fmt.Printf("Workers: %d (%T)\n", workers, workers)`.
hints: Use `getEnv("WORKERS", "4")` to get the value, then parse it
Handle the error from Atoi — use a default if parsing fails

verification.failureMessage: Use strconv.Atoi to convert the string to int.

steps.title: Flag package basics
steps.description: Define flags for `--port` (int, default 8080) and `--mode` (string, default "dev") using the `flag` package. Parse them and print "Running on port X in Y mode".
hints: `flag.Parse()` must be called after defining all flags
Access values: `fmt.Printf("Running on port %d in %s mode", *port, *mode)`

verification.failureMessage: Call flag.Parse() after defining your flags.
